messages:
maria: Hey team — customer (AcmeAnalytics) reports Google + GitHub SSO failing during oauth callback. They get 'redirect_uri_mismatch' from Google and 'state_mismatch' from our callback handler for GitHub. They say it started after we rolled out the proxy change last week. Need quick triage.

kevin: Can you paste the exact error strings/screenshots they sent? Also want the redirect_uri they're sending and the registered callback in the OAuth app console.

maria: Sent screenshots, here's the important bits from the logs they attached: 
- Google error: "error=redirect_uri_mismatch&error_description=Invalid+redirect:+https%3A%2F%2Fa.example.com%2Fauth%2Fcallback%2Fgoogle"
- Our app log at callback: "state validation failed: expected=abc123 got= (empty)"
- GitHub exchange: "invalid_grant: code verifier mismatch"

alex: Quick suspicion: proxy strip/rewrite of trailing slash or host header mismatch. Commonly redirect_uri encoded by client doesn't match registered value exactly (scheme, host, port, path, trailing slash). Also PKCE mistakes for GitHub.

kevin: @maria can you confirm registered OAuth app callback values? Are there both http:// and https:// entries? Any port numbers?

maria: They registered: https://a.example.com/auth/callback/google (no trailing slash) and https://a.example.com/auth/callback/github. The client is sending https://a.example.com/auth/callback/google/ (NOTE extra trailing slash). They confirmed that their client lives behind our new edge proxy which rewrites paths.

lucy: Also check SameSite cookie changes — state is usually stored in a session cookie. If the proxy updated cookie attributes (SameSite=None; Secure), older browsers or cross-site requests might drop the cookie -> state empty.

maria: Good catch. Customer is using Chrome and opens the auth flow in a new tab from an iframe — looks like the auth flow is cross-site. Cookie was set with SameSite=Lax previously by the app; proxy added a header that changed behavior.

alex: For PKCE "code verifier mismatch": often causes are: client uses plain instead of S256, code_verifier is truncated by URL encoding, or code_challenge computed incorrectly (Base64 vs Base64URL or padding included). Share the code_challenge from their initial /authorize request (should be S256 if code_challenge_method=S256).

maria: They sent the /authorize query string. For GitHub they have code_challenge=E9b...== and code_challenge_method=S256. The challenge contains '=' padding. GitHub docs expect base64url (no padding).

kevin: That will fail the exchange: server computes base64url(SHA256(code_verifier)) without padding and compares. If the client sent standard base64 with padding, mismatch. Quick fix: update client PKCE encoding or accept padded form (not recommended).

oauth-bot: Auth provider response captured: {"provider":"github","error":"invalid_grant","detail":"code_verifier did not match"} — logged at 2026-03-10T14:07:22Z

maria: Action items I'm doing now: 1) ask customer to change redirect to registered exact value (remove trailing slash) OR update app registration; 2) ask them to ensure PKCE challenge uses URL-safe base64 (no padding) and S256; 3) check our proxy cookie headers and SameSite attributes.

alex: Add repro steps for us to validate quickly. I recommend: 
1) Simulate auth request with exact redirect_uri (including trailing slash) to see Google error:
```
GET https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth?client_id=...&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fa.example.com%2Fauth%2Fcallback%2Fgoogle%2F&response_type=code&scope=openid%20email&state=xyz
```
2) For PKCE verify code_challenge generation locally: 
```
# python snippet
import hashlib, base64
verifier = b'my-secret-verifier'
h = hashlib.sha256(verifier).digest()
challenge = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(h).rstrip(b'=')
print(challenge.decode())
```
3) Reproduce GitHub exchange and watch our callback log for "state validation failed" and cookie value.

maria: Customer is low-priv and can't change OAuth app settings easily; asked if we can add a fallback.

lucy: Fallback risky. Do NOT accept mismatched redirect_uri. We can add clearer error UI/instructions and temporary guidance: ask the customer to update registered callback to the exact URI (including trailing slash) or change client to use registered URI. If SameSite is the issue, we can update cookie attributes on our side to SameSite=None; Secure and make sure auth requests are top-level navigations where possible.

kevin: I spun up a quick test matching their setup. Reproduced both errors: Google returns redirect_uri_mismatch when trailing slash differs; our session cookie not being sent in cross-site tab causes empty state. Also reproduced code_verifier mismatch if client uses standard base64 with padding.

maria: Proposed communication to customer: 
- Explain exact causes (redirect_uri must match exactly, PKCE must be base64url no padding, state stored in cookie needs SameSite=None for cross-site). Provide them repro snippets and exact fix steps. 
- If they cannot change app registration, suggest a temporary canonical redirect route they can use (we can map /auth/callback/google/ -> /auth/callback/google without breaking state) but need eng's signoff.

alex: Mapping is doable but touches security surface — would require strict whitelist and exact-match table. I can prototype a mapping that 301s to canonical path and preserves query params, but we must ensure we don't accept arbitrary redirect_uri values.

lucy: If we implement mapping, log and alert mismatched redirect_uri attempts and record client_id. Also require an allowlist maintained by product for exceptions.

maria: Customer also asked whether we can rotate OAuth client credentials if secret could have leaked during debug.

lucy: Yes, rotate (delete old secret and create a new one) and update their client config. Also recommend short-lived client secret where supported.

kevin: Next steps: 
- maria: send customer precise checklist + repro snippets (I gave a draft).
- alex: prototype safe redirect mapping and open PR for review (label security).
- lucy: prepare rotation guidance and security blurb.
- I'll add a telemetry alert to detect state empty + callback errors to catch other customers.

maria: Sending draft to customer now. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
